findings.description: The new count includes deleted tracked files because git ls-files reads the index rather than checking which files exist. Deleting a tracked .claude file therefore leaves ACTUAL_COUNT unchanged and suppresses the integrity mismatch that the previous filesystem count detected.
findings.failure_mode: In a Git-backed installation, a missing System Zone script or configuration file passes this integrity check, allowing preflight to proceed without its previous warning even though subsequent commands may fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Count tracked paths that still exist on disk, or explicitly detect deleted tracked paths before comparing counts. Perform this check in MANIFEST_TREE to preserve submodule support.

findings.description: In a submodule mount (.loa/.claude is a directory), any manifest path that is absent under .claude/ but present under .loa/ is now counted as informational 'not-mounted' and never fails. The check cannot distinguish 'intentionally not linked by this mount' from 'a linked fence file (hook, guard script, rule) was deleted or unlinked'. Before this change every absent manifest path was a hard Missing failure.
findings.failure_mode: An agent or operator removes e.g. .claude/hooks/implement-gate.sh or a .claude/rules/*.md symlink in a submodule-mounted downstream; check-loa.sh reports 'Integrity verified' plus a one-line not-mounted count and exits 0, so the deletion of a security fence is no longer surfaced.
findings.suggested_fix: Consult the mount scope (the set of paths the mount is supposed to link; tests/unit/check-loa-mount-scope.bats implies one exists) and treat an absent path that IS in scope as Missing (fail), reserving the informational outcome for paths genuinely outside the mount's scope. At minimum list the not-mounted paths instead of a bare count so deletions are visible.

findings.description: The function now ends with an unconditional `return 0`. Previously its exit status was that of `[[ "$drift" == "false" ]] && log ...`, i.e. 1 when any file was Tampered or Missing. If the caller (or `set -e`) relied on that return value rather than on a counter maintained by `fail`, tampered files no longer affect the script's exit code.
findings.failure_mode: check-loa.sh prints 'Tampered: ...' lines but exits 0, so CI or preflight gating on its exit code passes a modified System Zone.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify that `fail` increments a global error counter that the script's final exit uses; if it does not, keep the drift status as the function's return (`[[ "$drift" == "false" ]]`) or propagate it explicitly.

findings.description: The whole MODELINV ledger ($MINV, every eval/model-invoke.jsonl row with payloads), every envelope, DOT_WRITES and pipeline.json are passed to a single jq invocation as individual `--argjson` command-line arguments. Linux caps one argv string at MAX_ARG_STRLEN (128 KiB). A full pipeline run (plan/implement/review/audit/fix phases with multiple Flatline voices) can produce a model-invoke.jsonl larger than that.
findings.failure_mode: jq fails with 'Argument list too long' (E2BIG); under `set -e` the script exits non-zero and no runs.jsonl row is appended for that run, so the batch silently loses rows for exactly the longest, most expensive runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Write $MINV (and the other large inputs) to temp files and pass them with `--slurpfile`/`--rawfile`, or feed the ledger on stdin and read the rest via `$__loc__`-free file args; keep only small scalars as `--arg`.

findings.description: `ms(ts)` strips a fractional-seconds suffix and then calls `fromdateiso8601`, which only accepts `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`. Any pipeline.json `started`/`finished` value with a numeric offset (e.g. `+00:00` from `date -Iseconds`), a space separator, or no `Z` makes jq raise an error and the entire row build aborts (the row build is one jq program and the script runs under `set -e`).
findings.failure_mode: A run whose pipeline.json timestamps are not exactly `...Z` produces no runs.jsonl row at all, instead of a row with a fallback wall_clock_ms, and the batch runner sees a non-zero exit from ablation-row.sh.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the parse: `def ms(ts): if ts == null then null else ((ts | sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | try fromdateiso8601 catch null) as $s | if $s == null then null else $s * 1000 end) end;` and fall back to the summed phase durations when either endpoint fails to parse. Add a bats case with an offset timestamp.

findings.description: gpt-6.1-sol ships with gpt-5.5 prices explicitly marked PLACEHOLDER in a YAML comment only. The entry is also added to VALID_FLATLINE_MODELS and the generated registries, so it can be invoked directly over http_api; those ledger rows will carry `pricing_source: config` with `usage_source: actual` and nothing marks the cost as provisional. spend.sh caps and MODELINV cost reports therefore treat the placeholder as confirmed pricing.
findings.failure_mode: If the real gpt-6.1 rate card differs, every cost figure, spend cap decision and ablation cost_usd computed before the rate card is confirmed is wrong with no machine-readable indication, and cannot be re-priced after the fact without knowing which rows used the placeholder.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a machine-readable marker on the entry (e.g. `pricing: { ..., status: placeholder }` or `pricing_confirmed: false`) that find_pricing surfaces into ledger rows (e.g. `pricing_status`), and have spend.sh/validate-suite treat placeholder-priced models as estimated. Close the bead when the rate card is confirmed.
